content: The herb He Shou Wu (Polygonum multiflorum, also known as Fo-ti) has specific dosing recommendations depending on its intended use. For raw herb preparations, the recommended dosage is 9–15 grams. It is commonly used as an adaptogen, for alleviating constipation, and for its purported anti-aging properties. Drug Interactions: Fo-ti has been shown to enhance the effects of several medications through pharmacodynamic synergism. These include: 1. Antidiabetic Medications: Fo-ti may increase the effects of acarbose, glimepiride, glipizide, glyburide, metformin, miglitol, nateglinide, pioglitazone, repaglinide, rosiglitazone, saxagliptin, sitagliptin, and vildagliptin. It may also enhance the effects of various types of insulin, including insulin aspart, detemir, glargine, glulisine, lispro, NPH, and regular human insulin. The clinical significance of these interactions is currently unknown. 2. Antihypertensive Medications: Fo-ti may increase the effects of amlodipine, clevidipine, diltiazem, felodipine, isradipine, nicardipine, nifedipine, nisoldipine, and verapamil. The clinical significance of these interactions is also unknown. 3. Diuretics: Fo-ti may enhance the effects of bendroflumethiazide, bumetanide, chlorothiazide, chlorthalidone, cyclopenthiazide, ethacrynic acid, furosemide, hydrochlorothiazide, indapamide, methyclothiazide, metolazone, and torsemide. These interactions may theoretically increase the risk of hypokalemia (low potassium levels), although this risk is not well-documented. Adverse Effects: Gastrointestinal Effects: Fo-ti may cause diarrhea in some individuals. Neurological Effects: High doses of Fo-ti have been associated with paresthesia (a tingling or pins and needles sensation). Pregnancy and Lactation: Pregnancy: There is no established pregnancy category for Fo-ti. However, it is generally considered acceptable, as controlled studies in pregnant women have not shown evidence of fetal risk. Lactation: There is no available data regarding the safety of Fo-ti during lactation. Cost Information: No specific cost information is provided for Fo-ti. In summary, while Fo-ti is generally considered safe and has potential therapeutic benefits, its interactions with various medications and the theoretical risk of hypokalemia warrant caution. It is advisable to consult a healthcare provider before using Fo-ti, especially for individuals taking medications for diabetes, hypertension, or fluid retention.
